# Neural network

This script gives the following results for the neural network, separately for the aligned Big Five scores and the BFI-S items: the nested cross-validated performance, the selected hyperparameters, the training-set and hold-out performance, and the SHAP values for the hold-out set. The performance tables, the final models, and the SHAP results are saved, so the SHAP figure scripts can read them and the results can be checked without refitting.

## Modelling sample

The cleaning below is the same code as in Han and gives the same modelling sample as in the other analysis scripts.

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(tidymodels)
library(brulee)
library(future)
library(fastshap)

# The aligned data are loaded.
load("covid_aligned_BFF.RData")

# Country, gender, and education are stored as factors.
data_NEU.aligned$Country<-as.factor(data_NEU.aligned$Country)
data_NEU.aligned$Dem_gender<-as.factor(data_NEU.aligned$Dem_gender)
data_NEU.aligned$Dem_edu<-as.factor(data_NEU.aligned$Dem_edu)

# Rows with missing age, gender, or education are removed.
data<-data_NEU.aligned[
  !is.na(data_NEU.aligned$Dem_age)&
  !is.na(data_NEU.aligned$Dem_edu)&
  !is.na(data_NEU.aligned$Dem_gender),]

# Country is recoded to numbers and stored as a factor. The models use this version.
data$country<-as.numeric(data$Country)
data$country<-as.factor(data$country)
```

## Data splits

The split below is the same participant-level split as in the other analyses. The nested cross-validation and the final tuning are done inside the training set. The hold-out set is used only for the final performance and the SHAP values (Methods section).

```{r}
# This seed gives the same split as in the other analysis scripts.
set.seed(17)

# The participants are divided into a training set with 80% and a hold-out set with 20%.
data_split <- group_initial_split(data, group = ID, prop = 0.8)
train_set <- training(data_split)
holdout_set <- testing(data_split)

# The training set is divided into five outer folds, and each outer training portion into ten inner folds.
nested_folds <- nested_cv(
  train_set,
  outside = group_vfold_cv(group = ID, v = 5),
  inside = group_vfold_cv(group = ID, v = 10)
)

# The sample sizes of the training set and the hold-out set are printed.
nrow(train_set)
nrow(holdout_set)
```

## Model specification

```{r}
# Specify neural network model
nnet_model <- mlp(
  hidden_units = tune(),
  epochs = 100,
  learn_rate = tune(),
  penalty = tune(),
  dropout = 0,
  activation = "relu"
) %>%
  set_mode("regression") %>%
  set_engine(
    "brulee_two_layer",
    hidden_units_2 = tune(),
    activation_2 = "relu",
    optimizer = "ADAMw",
    batch_size = 128,
    stop_iter = 10
  )

# The recipe standardises the numeric predictors and dummy-codes the categorical predictors.
nnet_trait_recipe <- recipe(Compliance_2 ~ NEU + EXT + OPE + AGR + CON
  + Dem_age + Dem_edu + Dem_gender + country, data = train_set) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

# Combine specified model and recipe into a workflow
nnet_trait_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(nnet_trait_recipe) %>%
  add_model(nnet_model)

# Grid for hyperparameter tuning
nnet_trait_grid <- expand_grid(
  hidden_units = c(32, 64, 128),
  hidden_units_2 = c(32, 64, 128),
  learn_rate = c(0.0001, 0.001, 0.01),
  penalty = c(0.00001, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01)
)
```

## Nested cross-validation (aligned Big Five scores)

```{r}
# The training metrics of the outer folds are collected in this list.
nnet_trait_outer_training_folds <- list()

# In each outer fold, the hyperparameters are tuned in the inner folds and the selected pipeline is scored on the outer validation fold and the outer training portion.
nnet_trait_outer_validation <- map_dfr(seq_along(nested_folds$splits), function(i) {
  inner_folds <- nested_folds$inner_resamples[[i]]
  outer_split <- nested_folds$splits[[i]]
  
  # A separate seed is set for each outer fold, and the candidate combinations are evaluated in parallel in ten R sessions.
  set.seed(17 + i)
  plan("multisession", workers = 10)
  
  # The hyperparameters are tuned in the ten inner folds of the outer training portion.
  tuning_results <- tune_grid(
    nnet_trait_workflow,
    resamples = inner_folds,
    grid = nnet_trait_grid,
    metrics = yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::rmse))
  
  # The combination with the lowest mean RMSE is selected.
  best_params <- select_best(tuning_results, metric = "rmse")
  
  # The selected pipeline is fitted to the outer training portion and scored on the outer validation fold.
  outer_res <- last_fit(
    finalize_workflow(nnet_trait_workflow, best_params),
    split = outer_split,
    metrics = yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::rmse, yardstick::rsq_trad, yardstick::mae))
  
  # The outer training portion is divided into the predictors and general compliance.
  analysis_set <- analysis(outer_split)
  analysis_x <- select(analysis_set, -Compliance_2)
  analysis_truth <- select(analysis_set, Compliance_2)

  # RMSE, MAE, and R2 are calculated for the outer training portion.
  analysis_metrics <- predict(
    outer_res$.workflow[[1]],
    new_data = analysis_x) %>%
    bind_cols(analysis_truth) %>%
    yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::rmse, yardstick::rsq_trad, yardstick::mae)(
      truth = Compliance_2,
      estimate = .pred)
  
  # The training metrics are stored for this outer fold.
  nnet_trait_outer_training_folds[[i]] <<- mutate(analysis_metrics, outer_fold = i)

  # The validation metrics are returned with the selected hyperparameters.
  outer_res$.metrics[[1]] %>%
    mutate(
      outer_fold = i,
      best_hidden_units = best_params$hidden_units,
      best_hidden_units_2 = best_params$hidden_units_2,
      best_learn_rate = best_params$learn_rate,
      best_penalty = best_params$penalty
    )
})

# The training metrics of the five outer folds are combined.
nnet_trait_outer_training <- bind_rows(nnet_trait_outer_training_folds)

# The validation metrics and the training metrics are saved.
saveRDS(nnet_trait_outer_validation, "nnet_trait_outer_validation.rds")
saveRDS(nnet_trait_outer_training, "nnet_trait_outer_training.rds")

# The parallel sessions are closed.
plan("sequential")
```

### Outer validation performance (aligned Big Five scores)

```{r}
# The mean and standard deviation of the validation metrics are calculated across the five outer folds.
nnet_trait_outer_validation %>%
  group_by(.metric) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(.estimate), sd = sd(.estimate), .groups = "drop")

# The validation metrics of each outer fold are printed.
print(nnet_trait_outer_validation)

# The hyperparameters selected in each outer fold are printed.
nnet_trait_outer_validation %>%
  distinct(
    outer_fold,
    best_hidden_units,
    best_hidden_units_2,
    best_learn_rate,
    best_penalty)
```

### Outer training performance (aligned Big Five scores)

```{r}
# The mean and standard deviation of the training metrics are calculated across the five outer folds.
nnet_trait_outer_training %>%
  group_by(.metric) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(.estimate),
    sd = sd(.estimate),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## Final model (aligned Big Five scores)

```{r}
# The complete training set is divided into ten folds for the final hyperparameter tuning.
set.seed(17)
nnet_trait_tuning_folds <- group_vfold_cv(train_set, group = ID, v = 10)

# The candidate combinations are evaluated in parallel in ten R sessions.
plan("multisession", workers = 10)

# The hyperparameters are tuned in the ten folds of the complete training set.
nnet_trait_tuning <- tune_grid(
  nnet_trait_workflow,
  resamples = nnet_trait_tuning_folds,
  grid = nnet_trait_grid,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::rmse)
)

# The combination with the lowest mean RMSE is selected.
nnet_trait_selected <- select_best(nnet_trait_tuning, metric = "rmse")
nnet_trait_selected

# The selected pipeline is fitted to the complete training set and saved.
nnet_trait_final_workflow <- finalize_workflow(nnet_trait_workflow, nnet_trait_selected)
nnet_trait_model <- fit(nnet_trait_final_workflow, data = train_set)
saveRDS(nnet_trait_model, "nnet_trait_model.rds")

# RMSE, MAE, and R2 are calculated for the training set and saved.
nnet_trait_training <- predict(nnet_trait_model, new_data = train_set) %>%
  bind_cols(select(train_set, Compliance_2)) %>%
  yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::rmse, yardstick::rsq_trad, yardstick::mae)(truth = Compliance_2, estimate = .pred)
nnet_trait_training
saveRDS(nnet_trait_training, "nnet_trait_training.rds")

# RMSE, MAE, and R2 are calculated for the hold-out set and saved.
nnet_trait_holdout <- predict(nnet_trait_model, new_data = holdout_set) %>%
  bind_cols(select(holdout_set, Compliance_2)) %>%
  yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::rmse, yardstick::rsq_trad, yardstick::mae)(truth = Compliance_2, estimate = .pred)

nnet_trait_holdout
saveRDS(nnet_trait_holdout, "nnet_trait_holdout.rds")

# The parallel sessions are closed.
plan("sequential")
```

## SHAP values (aligned Big Five scores)

```{r}
# The hold-out values of the predictors in the model are selected.
# For each hold-out participant, the SHAP value of each predictor is approximated with 50 Monte Carlo simulations.
set.seed(17)
nnet_trait_shap_data <- select(holdout_set, NEU, EXT, OPE, AGR, CON, Dem_age, Dem_edu, Dem_gender, country)
nnet_trait_shap_values <- fastshap::explain(
  object = nnet_trait_model,
  X = nnet_trait_shap_data,
  pred_wrapper = function(object, newdata) predict(object, new_data = newdata)$.pred,
  nsim = 50
)

# The importance of each predictor is its mean absolute SHAP value across the hold-out participants. The predictors are sorted from the most to the least important.
nnet_trait_shap_importance <- tibble(
  feature = colnames(nnet_trait_shap_values),
  mean_abs_shap = unname(colMeans(abs(nnet_trait_shap_values)))
) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_abs_shap))

# The five aligned scores are standardised with the training-set mean and standard deviation. Age, education, gender, and country are unchanged.
nnet_trait_shap_data_standardised <- nnet_trait_shap_data %>%
  mutate(across(
    c(NEU, EXT, OPE, AGR, CON),
    ~ (.x - mean(train_set[[cur_column()]], na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(train_set[[cur_column()]], na.rm = TRUE)
  ))

# The SHAP values, the hold-out predictor values they explain, the same values with standardised aligned scores, and the importance are saved.
saveRDS(nnet_trait_shap_values, "nnet_trait_shap_values.rds")
saveRDS(nnet_trait_shap_data, "nnet_trait_shap_data.rds")
saveRDS(nnet_trait_shap_data_standardised, "nnet_trait_shap_data_standardised.rds")
saveRDS(nnet_trait_shap_importance, "nnet_trait_shap_importance.rds")

# The importance is printed (Supplementary Figure S3).
nnet_trait_shap_importance
```

# BFI-S items

## Model specification

```{r}
# The recipe standardises the numeric predictors and dummy-codes the categorical predictors.
nnet_item_recipe <- recipe(
  Compliance_2 ~ BFF_15_1 + BFF_15_2 + BFF_15_3 +
    BFF_15_4 + BFF_15_5 + BFF_15_6 +
    BFF_15_7 + BFF_15_8 + BFF_15_9 +
    BFF_15_10 + BFF_15_11 + BFF_15_12 +
    BFF_15_13 + BFF_15_14 + BFF_15_15 +
    Dem_age + Dem_edu + Dem_gender + country,
  data = train_set
) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

# Combine specified model and recipe into a workflow
nnet_item_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(nnet_item_recipe) %>%
  add_model(nnet_model)

# Grid for hyperparameter tuning
nnet_item_grid <- expand_grid(
  hidden_units = c(32, 64, 128),
  hidden_units_2 = c(32, 64, 128),
  learn_rate = c(0.0001, 0.001, 0.01),
  penalty = c(0.00001, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01)
)
```

  # The outer training portion is divided into the predictors and general compliance.

  # The training metrics are stored for this outer fold.

  outer_res$.metrics[[1]] %>%

## Final model (BFI-S items)

```{r}
# The complete training set is divided into ten folds for the final hyperparameter tuning.
set.seed(17)
nnet_item_tuning_folds <- group_vfold_cv(train_set, group = ID, v = 10)

# The candidate combinations are evaluated in parallel in ten R sessions.
plan("multisession", workers = 10)

# The hyperparameters are tuned in the ten folds of the complete training set.
nnet_item_tuning <- tune_grid(
  nnet_item_workflow,
  resamples = nnet_item_tuning_folds,
  grid = nnet_item_grid,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::rmse)
)

# The combination with the lowest mean RMSE is selected.
nnet_item_selected <- select_best(nnet_item_tuning, metric = "rmse")
nnet_item_selected

# The selected pipeline is fitted to the complete training set and saved.
nnet_item_final_workflow <- finalize_workflow(nnet_item_workflow, nnet_item_selected)
nnet_item_model <- fit(nnet_item_final_workflow, data = train_set)
saveRDS(nnet_item_model, "nnet_item_model.rds")

# RMSE, MAE, and R2 are calculated for the training set and saved.
nnet_item_training <- predict(nnet_item_model, new_data = train_set) %>%
  bind_cols(select(train_set, Compliance_2)) %>%
  yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::rmse, yardstick::rsq_trad, yardstick::mae)(truth = Compliance_2, estimate = .pred)
nnet_item_training
saveRDS(nnet_item_training, "nnet_item_training.rds")

# RMSE, MAE, and R2 are calculated for the hold-out set and saved.
nnet_item_holdout <- predict(nnet_item_model, new_data = holdout_set) %>%
  bind_cols(select(holdout_set, Compliance_2)) %>%
  yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::rmse, yardstick::rsq_trad, yardstick::mae)(truth = Compliance_2, estimate = .pred)

nnet_item_holdout
saveRDS(nnet_item_holdout, "nnet_item_holdout.rds")

# The parallel sessions are closed.
plan("sequential")
```

## SHAP values (BFI-S items)

```{r}
# The hold-out values of the predictors in the model are selected.
# For each hold-out participant, the SHAP value of each predictor is approximated with 50 Monte Carlo simulations.
set.seed(17)
nnet_item_shap_data <- select(holdout_set, all_of(paste0("BFF_15_", 1:15)), Dem_age, Dem_edu, Dem_gender, country)
nnet_item_shap_values <- fastshap::explain(
  object = nnet_item_model,
  X = nnet_item_shap_data,
  pred_wrapper = function(object, newdata) predict(object, new_data = newdata)$.pred,
  nsim = 50
)

# The importance of each predictor is its mean absolute SHAP value across the hold-out participants. The predictors are sorted from the most to the least important.
nnet_item_shap_importance <- tibble(
  feature = colnames(nnet_item_shap_values),
  mean_abs_shap = unname(colMeans(abs(nnet_item_shap_values)))
) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_abs_shap))

# The 15 item scores are standardised with the training-set mean and standard deviation. Age, education, gender, and country are unchanged.
nnet_item_shap_data_standardised <- nnet_item_shap_data %>%
  mutate(across(
    all_of(paste0("BFF_15_", 1:15)),
    ~ (.x - mean(train_set[[cur_column()]], na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(train_set[[cur_column()]], na.rm = TRUE)
  ))

# The SHAP values, the hold-out predictor values they explain, the same values with standardised item scores, and the importance are saved.
saveRDS(nnet_item_shap_values, "nnet_item_shap_values.rds")
saveRDS(nnet_item_shap_data, "nnet_item_shap_data.rds")
saveRDS(nnet_item_shap_data_standardised, "nnet_item_shap_data_standardised.rds")
saveRDS(nnet_item_shap_importance, "nnet_item_shap_importance.rds")

# The importance is printed (Supplementary Table S8).
nnet_item_shap_importance
```
